newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore ethylene complex to restart this week.
newsitem.headline: Singapore ethylene complex to restart this week.

text.p: The Petrochemical Corporation of Singapore (PCS) said on Wednesday its new 515,000 tonne per year ethylene plant will restart this week after it was shutdown on April 28 following mechanical problems.
PCS also said that key downstream units including a polyethylene and polypropylene plant, and a styrene monomer/propylene oxide plant will also restart this week.
"Operations will resume this week and on-specification ethylene is expected a few days later," PCS said in reply to a Reuters' query.
The new plant, which is at the centre of a Singapore $3.4 billion (US$ 2.36 billion) petrochemical complex, began producing on-specification ethylene over the weekend of April 19.
"Our cracker was shut down on April 28. We had minor problems such as plugging of filters and they have been rectified," PCS said.
As a result of the shutdown to the ethylene plant, key derivative plants were also closed, PCS said.
PCS is a 50:50 joint venture between Royal Dutch Shell and a Sumitomo Chemical led consortium of Japanese companies.
The Polyethylene Co (TPC), a 53-percent subsidiary of Sumitomo Chemicals which began producing on-specification product at the same time as PCS, was also closed.
The new TPC plant will produce 190,000 tonnes per year of polyethylene and 120,000 tonnes of polypropylene.
Another plant that has been affected by the shutdown of PCS's ethylene plant is the 450,000 tonne per year styrene monomer/propylene oxide plant.
The plant, a 70-percent subsidiary of Shell, was due to start up in end April but this was delayed to late this week.
